title: Homology comparison for the explicit ideal-layer tensor complex
statement: Let X be any scheme, (A,I) an adic coefficient datum, phi a compatible family of constant-to-actual finite coefficient isomorphisms as in [def-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-quotient-model-data], M a derived completed-coefficient object, n a natural number, and Z an etale chart. Let P be a bounded-above cochain complex of projective A/I^1-modules. Suppose the residue reduction of M on Z is isomorphic to the constant realization of P transported by phi_0. Let T_n(P) be the explicit ideal-layer tensor complex of [def-weil-pbc-finite-quotient-layer-tensor-complex]. Then in every integer degree q the homology of the actual layer object [def-weil-pbc-finite-quotient-coefficient-layer-data], restricted to Z, is isomorphic to the ordinary constant realization [def-weil-pbc-finite-coefficient-local-homology-models] of H^q(T_n(P)), transported by phi_{n+1} and restricted to Z. No lower support bound, finite-generation hypothesis on P, compactness, or local Noetherian hypothesis on X is required.

source.place: Tag 094I, lemma-locally-constant-bounded, the displayed ideal-layer balancing identity; Tag 094H, lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product.

proof.text: Identify the explicit ideal-layer module with the algebraic quotient-map kernel. Exact constant realization and the compatible coefficient isomorphisms identify its sheaf realization, with its retained successor-ring action, with kernel(finiteQuotientUnitMap).

Derived tensor balancing writes the layer as the residue reduction derived-tensored with the ideal layer, and restricted back to successor coefficients. Exact slice restriction commutes with this comparison. Apply the given residue-model isomorphism on the slice.

The bounded-above projective complex computes derived tensor by ordinary termwise tensor. Under exact constant realization its differential is 1 tensor d_P, exactly the constructed tensor complex. Exact constants, coefficient transport along an isomorphism, and exact slice restriction commute with homology. Thus the localized homology of the layer is the constant realization of the explicit complex homology. Neither finite generation nor a lower bound is used.

theorem finiteQuotient_layer_tensor_homology_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t})
    {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    [∀ n : ℕ, (koszulConstantFunctor X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))).PreservesZeroMorphisms]
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, adicConstantRing X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)) ⟶
      completedAdicFiniteCommRing X d n)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (φ n))
    (hcompat : FinitePerfectModelsCompatible X d φ)
    (M : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules X d))
    (b : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (Z : X.Etale)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (0 + 1))) ℤ)
    (hPb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (0 + 1)) (P.X i))
    (e : Nonempty
      (ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses (completedAdicFiniteRing X d 0)
          ((toProEt X).obj Z) ((completedAdicQuotientReduction X d 0).obj M) ≅
        ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses (completedAdicFiniteRing X d 0)
          ((toProEt X).obj Z) ((completedAdicDerivedChange X (φ 0)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (finiteModelConstantComplex X _ P))))) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ ((toProEt X).obj Z)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
            (finiteQuotientLayerObject X d M n)) ≅
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ ((toProEt X).obj Z)).obj
          ((finiteCoefficientConstantFunctor X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1 + 1))
            (φ (n + 1))).obj ((finiteQuotientLayerTensorComplex d.ideal n P).homology q)))
